sources.title: Here’s how to make that new Black Friday TV look its best

extraction.body: But once you get a new one home and set it up in your living room, it might not meet expectations when you turn it on. Maybe it’s overly bright, or things just look… off. Luckily, there are some easy tweaks you can make so that new, expensive purchase looks its best. It seems counterintuitive, but the default mode for most TVs out of the box isn’t accurate and can include lots of extra processing that makes the image look artificially detailed or overly smooth. The easiest way to make the biggest positive change to your TV’s image is by changing out of this picture mode. Using Filmmaker, Movie, Cinema, or Professional picture mode (each company uses different names) will make the color temperature more accurate — it will look more red in comparison to the very blue Eco mode, but trust me, it’s far more realistic — and will either turn off extra processing or, at the very least, tone it down. Also, avoid Vivid and Dynamic modes, which are only there to blast brightness and make the image incredibly blue. The idea behind it is solid — it adjusts the picture brightness and color temperature based on the ambient light in the room — but I have yet to find one that doesn’t make distracting brightness adjustments while I’m watching TV. This can be done with the brightness or backlight slider, whichever one looks like it changes the brightness across the entire screen. It’s quite often referred to as the “soap opera effect” because it makes movies look like afternoon TV dramas. Using Filmmaker mode will generally turn this and other extraneous processing off, but it’s still best to double-check. If you plan on gaming, using Gaming mode will turn off some of that extra processing to reduce input lag as much as possible, and to make high refresh rate modes available. I recommend looking for the color temperature setting and switching it to something with “warm” in the title, as that will move the color temp toward something more natural. Finally, if you have anything connected to your TV via HDMI (especially a gaming console), make sure the HDMI settings are set to Enhanced instead of Standard. As with the power settings, HDMI settings are usually found in a General menu and can be called HDMI signal format or External Device Manager. Getting a new TV is a big investment, and one that should last you a few years at least. And while most TVs today can perform incredibly well, they still need a bit of a nudge to get all the performance you paid for. Making these tweaks will do exactly that and lead to years of enjoyment.

extraction.body: Black Friday has arrived, and it's packed with record-low prices on some of my favorite TV models from Samsung, Roku, LG, Sony, TCL, and Hisense. I review TVs year-round, so I know just how expensive top models can get. But these Black Friday TV deals offer up to $3,000 off some of the best OLED, Mini LED, and RGB LED models my team and I have tested. If I had to pick just one Black Friday TV deal to recommend, it would be this all-time low price on the Samsung 65-inch S90H OLED. The S90H holds the top spot in my guide to the best TVs, delivering pixel-level contrast along with a highly effective anti-glare screen that's a game changer for rooms with lots of lamps and windows. This model is also available in a huge 98-inch size, which is on sale for $1,698, a nearly unrivaled value for such a massive Mini LED TV with these specs. The QM6K holds the top spot in my guide to the best budget TVs, beating most entry-level competitors with its solid local dimming and high 144Hz refresh rate for gaming. Below, you'll find all of the best Black Friday TV deals so far, focusing on models my team and I have put through our rigorous testing process. I've organized them all by brand and included multiple sizes for each model so you can pick the one that fits best. I'll be keeping an eye on more Black Friday TV discounts throughout the day and beyond, so check back for the latest deals. Check out our full roundup of all the best Black Friday deals. Some of the best Samsung TVs are on sale in the lead-up to Black Friday. Most notably, the S90H and the latest Frame TV are both getting excellent discounts, with many sizes at their lowest prices ever. The S90H is one of the most versatile TVs available and a top value for most needs, while the Frame is designed to look like a piece of art hanging on your wall when you're not using it. What we like What we don't like Samsung's Frame TV is designed to look like a piece of art on your wall thanks to its flush mount, matte screen, and magnetic frame bezels. This 2025 model uses a separate One Connect Box to house its inputs. What we like What we don't like The latest version of Samsung's Frame TV retains the core features we love, including a matte screen, interchangeable bezels, and access to Samsung's Art Store. But this year's model has its HDMI ports built in rather than housed in a separate box. What we like What we don't like The S95H is Samsung's 2026 flagship OLED TV, and it's one of the most impressive displays the brand has ever made. It boasts record-level brightness for an OLED and a unique frame-like design. What we like What we don't like The Frame Pro is a gallery-style TV with a brighter, higher-contrast image than Samsung's standard Frame model. What we like What we don't like LG makes some of my favorite OLED TVs, and its C6H and G6 are both getting excellent discounts. The C6H is my go-to recommendation for anyone who wants an extra-large OLED. This model is only sold in 77- and 83-inch sizes, and it delivers a noticeably brighter image than the smaller C6. Meanwhile, the G6 is LG's top-performing OLED, with an even brighter image and the ability to hang flush on your wall. The 65-inch model is down to $2,000 for Black Friday. For more info, head over to my LG C6H TV review and guide to the best LG TVs. What we like What we don't like The B6 is LG's entry-level OLED. It's dimmer than pricier models but still offers pixel-level contrast and wide viewing angles. What we like What we don't like The 77- and 83-inch sizes of LG's C6 OLED use a brighter panel than smaller models, giving them performance closer to the brand's high-end G Series. What we like What we don't like The C6 is LG's midrange OLED for 2026. What we like What we don't like Roku recently released its first-ever OLED TV models, and they launched at highly competitive prices. For Black Friday, they're an even better value, with the 55-inch model starting at just $700. That's one of the lowest prices I've ever seen on any OLED that size. That's not a record low, but it's still a good value for what you get. Roku's entry-level OLED TV combines all the perks of OLED panel technology, including pixel-level contrast and wide viewing angles, with Roku's easy to use intergace.

Amazon, Walmart and brands like HexClad and Our Place are dishing out major Black Friday deals on kitchen items, so you can replace old pans and dull knives for less. ($179, was $199) : Save $20 Bonsenkitchen Vacuum Sealer with Easy Handle Design ($74, was $100) : Save $26 HexClad Damascus Steel Knife Set, 7-Piece ($379, was $783) : Save $404 I'm a shopping editor with a decade of experience covering deals, so I know what makes a good sale. But I also checked in with Yahoo's resident professional baker, Britt Ross , for her expert take on what to add to your kitchen this season. She says countertop appliances, like KitchenAid stand mixers and Vitamix blenders , are often at their lowest prices of the year. For her own kitchen, she's eyeing this gorgeous Cuisinart 7-piece stainless steel cookware set (the brand topped our list of the best cookware) and a new Lodge Dutch oven . "They come in tons of beautiful colors, and the quality rivals that of the pricier brands," she says. Want more shopping inspo? Take a look below at the best Black Friday kitchen deals, including more of our pro baker's favorite finds. There's something satisfying about a matching kitchen setup. Even the most basic culinary tasks feel more grown-up, and your cabinets look like they belong to someone who has their life together (whether or not that's actually the case). This would also make a wonderful gift for someone just starting out. No mismatched hand-me-downs, random thrift-store finds or realizing halfway through making dinner that you don't own a decent baking dish. The well-reviewed set (now 60% off!) includes pots and pans, bakeware, tinted glass prep bowls, wooden utensils, a trivet, spoon rest and pot holders — a whopping 23 pieces in total. Basically, it's a whole kitchen starter kit wrapped up in one very pretty package. "My one complaint about my air fryer is that it's not big enough to cook a frozen pizza," laments Senior Writer Carrie McCabe . "Well, OK, one more critique: It also takes up a bit more room than I'd like. So I've got my eye on this one from Ninja. It's roomy enough for a 12-inch pizza, flips up on its back (let it cool first!) to save counter space and can bake, toast, dehydrate and roast in addition to air frying. One recent shopper said it 'could be the best air fryer [they've] ever had.'" (Psst: My parents own this model and couldn't be happier with it.) Good deal: A quality, cook-everything air fryer that can handle pizzas for $150? Sold. We've only seen this unit dip a few bucks lower this year, and that was months ago. Bakers and other folks with soft human hands, behold! A nearly-70% discount on our absolute favorite pair of oven mitts (and we tested a bunch before crowning a winner). These KitchenAid mitts performed well and looked good during testing, and our own Home Editor Elizabeth Berry has owned them for about six months. She loves the soft, quilted polyester lining and flexible silicone exterior, which makes it comfortable to grip pots and pans. Great time to buy: As little as $10 for the mitts that outperformed all others? Sold! If your current mitts are looking a little worse for wear, why not upgrade while these are so cheap? "This Crock-Pot classic is a 7-quart slow cooker that allows you to prep a recipe, set to cook, and return to a hot, ready-to-enjoy meal for 10 or more people," says McCabe. "That's sure to please Aunt Lucy, Uncle Dave, and anyone else in the fam staying over for Thanksgiving!" Can we also talk about that stunning blue hue? (It's also available in three other colors.) Great time to buy: At just $35 (from $80) and a rare near-60% off at Walmart, it's the lowest price we're seeing across the 'net and a no-brainer buy ahead of holiday hosting season. If you want to watch your food crisp up in real time, Cuisinart's air fryer is a smart pick. It has a 4-quart glass basket that heats up to 450°F to fry, bake, broil, recrisp and keep food warm. It's easy to use, and even comes with the option to customize two preset buttons so you can cook your go-to meal with one tap. Plus, it's 40% off for Black Friday, bringing the price down to less than $100. Senior Home Editor Jessica Dodell-Feder included this model in her roundup of the best Keurig coffee makers , saying it "gives you a single-serve and drip coffee maker in one." She adds, "When testing its single-serve capabilities, it brewed coffee that was some of the tastiest I've had from a Keurig. ... I preferred the 'strong' option, as there is a noticeable distinction between it and a regular brew (I personally think it tastes less bitter). When it came time to switch gears and brew a carafe, I found the programming to be excellent. I set the time I wanted the pot to start brewing, and even though I accidentally lifted the single-serve handle, it automatically switched back to carafe mode when the time came." Maybe you're cooking for two or just yourself. In that case, you might not need a huge air fryer taking up space in your kitchen, and this 4-quart device will do the trick. It has a small window to watch your food crisp up in real time, and in addition to air frying, it also bakes, roasts, broils, dehydrates and reheats foods with little to no preheating time. We recently named the 6-quart Vortex the best budget air fryer after testing more than 20 of these gadgets! If you don't have a food chopper, consider getting one before the holiday season. Take it from Ross: "This little whizzer is one of my most-reached-for kitchen gadgets, and it's still going strong at about a decade old. It's super compact but powerful enough to blitz almonds into nut butter in a jiffy. It's also perfect for pureeing vegetables into cold sauces and soups, emulsifying dressings, and I've even used it to make whipped cream when I don't feel like whisking by hand." Every home chef needs a solid set of knives . If you don't cook every day, you may not need them sitting in a knife block on your kitchen counter, but you still need something sharp to chop, slice and dice. This handy set includes six knives in various sizes, each with matching blade covers, plus a pair of kitchen shears. The ceramic blades are easy to clean, just make sure they're totally dry before you store them in their guards (this will help them last longer). Good deal: These knives go on sale frequently, but this is around the lowest price we've seen in a year. The reviews quoted above reflect the most recent versions at the time of publication. Bakers and other folks with soft human hands, behold! A nearly-70% discount on our absolute favorite pair of oven mitts (and we tested a bunch before crowning a winner). These KitchenAid mitts performed well and looked good during testing, and our own Home Editor Elizabeth Berry has owned them for about six months. She loves the soft, quilted polyester lining and flexible silicone exterior, which makes it comfortable to grip pots and pans.
Great time to buy: As little as $10 for the mitts that outperformed all others? Sold! If your current mitts are looking a little worse for wear, why not upgrade while these are so cheap?

"This Crock-Pot classic is a 7-quart slow cooker that allows you to prep a recipe, set to cook, and return to a hot, ready-to-enjoy meal for 10 or more people," says McCabe. "That's sure to please Aunt Lucy, Uncle Dave, and anyone else in the fam staying over for Thanksgiving!" Can we also talk about that stunning blue hue? (It's also available in three other colors.)
Great time to buy: At just $35 (from $80) and a rare near-60% off at Walmart, it's the lowest price we're seeing across the 'net and a no-brainer buy ahead of holiday hosting season.

If you want to watch your food crisp up in real time, Cuisinart's air fryer is a smart pick. It has a 4-quart glass basket that heats up to 450°F to fry, bake, broil, recrisp and keep food warm. It's easy to use, and even comes with the option to customize two preset buttons so you can cook your go-to meal with one tap. Plus, it's 40% off for Black Friday, bringing the price down to less than $100.

Senior Home Editor Jessica Dodell-Feder included this model in her roundup of the best Keurig coffee makers , saying it "gives you a single-serve and drip coffee maker in one." She adds, "When testing its single-serve capabilities, it brewed coffee that was some of the tastiest I've had from a Keurig. ... I preferred the 'strong' option, as there is a noticeable distinction between it and a regular brew (I personally think it tastes less bitter). When it came time to switch gears and brew a carafe, I found the programming to be excellent. I set the time I wanted the pot to start brewing, and even though I accidentally lifted the single-serve handle, it automatically switched back to carafe mode when the time came."

Maybe you're cooking for two or just yourself. In that case, you might not need a huge air fryer taking up space in your kitchen, and this 4-quart device will do the trick. It has a small window to watch your food crisp up in real time, and in addition to air frying, it also bakes, roasts, broils, dehydrates and reheats foods with little to no preheating time. We recently named the 6-quart Vortex the best budget air fryer after testing more than 20 of these gadgets!

If you don't have a food chopper, consider getting one before the holiday season. Take it from Ross: "This little whizzer is one of my most-reached-for kitchen gadgets, and it's still going strong at about a decade old. It's super compact but powerful enough to blitz almonds into nut butter in a jiffy. It's also perfect for pureeing vegetables into cold sauces and soups, emulsifying dressings, and I've even used it to make whipped cream when I don't feel like whisking by hand."

Every home chef needs a solid set of knives . If you don't cook every day, you may not need them sitting in a knife block on your kitchen counter, but you still need something sharp to chop, slice and dice. This handy set includes six knives in various sizes, each with matching blade covers, plus a pair of kitchen shears. The ceramic blades are easy to clean, just make sure they're totally dry before you store them in their guards (this will help them last longer).
Good deal: These knives go on sale frequently, but this is around the lowest price we've seen in a year.

It’s also an opportunity to knock out your holiday shopping in one fell swoop - preferably before December sneaks up on you (it somehow always does). We spent months testing and handpicking 145 presents for our ultimate holiday gift guide , from cozy knits to shiny kitchen gadgets to delightful little stocking stuffers. Now, we’ve rounded up our favorites on sale, so you can check off everyone on your list without paying full price. The chef’s knife, serrated knife and paring knife cover the needs of most home cooks – and after more than a year of near-daily use, the Japanese steel blades on all three are still sharp. It’s a great starter set or starting-over set, and it’s available with a magnetic knife stand or without. Emily Farris People spend more time in pyjamas than most clothes, so a decent set is an investment in the care and comfort of those you love. These Cozy Earth bamboo stretch-knit pajamas are wonderfully cozy, with a flexible fit and a wonderful feeling of smooth luxury. The breathable bamboo fabric also keeps things cool on a warm night. Richard Baguley Juno DeMelo, a Filter contributor, does not leave home without one of these tiny tins of Jacobsen sea salt from Oregon. “I keep one in our camping bin and another in my purse so I can dial in the salt level of whatever I’m eating no matter where in the world I am,” she wrote. Karen Yuan “That seems to be popular. I think everyone, mostly friends at school, wants to listen to music, and they are just the popular brand,” said Ollie, a 17-year-old. Lauren Gould In testing, the Mzoo sleep mask beat out 31 competitors to become our overall favorite, then went on to become one of our most popular recommendations of all time (our readers are a sleepy bunch). It gives total blackout coverage and stays comfortable enough to wear all night or a whole plane flight. Karen Yuan $20 $26 at Amazon , $21 $45 at Kitsch Satin pillowcases help keep your skin smooth and your hair undamaged. This one from Kitsch is available in a Galactic Empire or Rebel Alliance theme, depending on your political orientation to the Force. Richard Baguley If you know someone who desperately needs a spa day but can never find the time, bring the spa to them. The Parachute organic super plush towels are some of the best bath towels we have ever tested. Made of thick, squishy organic Turkish cotton, Parachute’s towels are soft from edge to edge, giving you a sense of coziness that other towel brands struggle to match. Jon Chan Between wildfire smoke and pollution, air quality is a rising concern. If you are interested in giving the gift of clean air to a loved one, this Shark NeverChange air purifier is one of the best air purifiers I have tested, with a Hepa and carbon filter that can last up to five years. Jon Chan $18 $26 at Chewy , Amazon I switched to this elevated dish after Tux kept managing to push his lightweight bowl under a nearby bar cart. This sturdier bowl stays put more easily and means less crouching for a more comfortable mealtime. Tracy Allison Any Anthropologie employee knows about the Alani sweater – and anyone who receives this as a gift will be happy to – whether it be your stylish mom, in-law or friend who hates spending money on themselves. Even after testing far pricier sweaters, I still have not found something softer than this one. While I have a crewneck version that’s not currently sold, the mockneck design is an equally great gift. It’s also not too heavy, which makes it a wonderful transition piece come spring. Lauren Gould I have had my Dyson blowdryer for several years with no signs of needing to replace it. But as time and tech have moved on, the brand’s latest versions have new features such as “pause detect mode”, “attachment learning” and “scalp protect mode”. This model, the Dyson Supersonic Nural hairdryer, comes with the aforementioned bells and whistles as well as five magnetic attachments for different styling needs (to smooth flyaways, pouf up curls, concentrate air flow and detangle). Give this to someone whose janky old drugstore hairdryer is on the fritz – it’s worth it. Maria Ricapito Kari Traa is perhaps the best-known name in women’s base layers and for good reason. The fun patterns and colors give women a chance to show off their style. The Smekker is one of my favorite layers to wear during my 50-plus ski days each season in Aspen because I can take it from the chairlift to the après and still look good. Heather Balogh Rochfort $262 $350 at Mountain Hardwear (men’s), (women’s) Mountain Hardwear’s hooded jacket is like yoga pants for your arms. You get the warmth of a down jacket, but it is super stretchy thanks to flexible fabric and welded (instead of stitched) seams. I have broader shoulders and it makes the jacket far more comfortable when I am hiking. Heather Balogh Rochfort Touchland’s tween-endorsed bestseller from last year’s gift guide is still popular in 2026. When I recently gave my nine-year-old cousin one from Amazon’s beauty Advent calendar, it caused far more excitement than you would think for a hand sanitizer. Lauren Gould If you want to browse more Black Friday 2026 deals yourself, the links below lead directly to each major retailer’s holiday deals homepage. Check out our many buying guides and holiday gift guides for more ideas. We work for our readers, rather than the brands we write about. Every item we recommend is something a Filter editor or contributor has personally tested and can vouch for unless stated otherwise. On occasion, we may present a close substitute from the same brand and explain any differences from the original. (So while we love sharing good deals, we also aren’t afraid to call out the unimpressive ones.) Our mission is to help you filter out junk products and buy fewer, better things. We also consider possible impacts on your health or the environment in our coverage and companies cannot purchase a spot in our product rankings because we are here to serve you, not corporations.

But I also checked in with Yahoo's resident professional baker, Britt Ross , for her expert take on what to add to your kitchen this season. She says countertop appliances, like KitchenAid stand mixers and Vitamix blenders , are often at their lowest prices of the year. "They come in tons of beautiful colors, and the quality rivals that of the pricier brands," she says. Want more shopping inspo? Take a look below at the best Black Friday kitchen deals, including more of our pro baker's favorite finds. There's something satisfying about a matching kitchen setup. Even the most basic culinary tasks feel more grown-up, and your cabinets look like they belong to someone who has their life together (whether or not that's actually the case). This would also make a wonderful gift for someone just starting out. No mismatched hand-me-downs, random thrift-store finds or realizing halfway through making dinner that you don't own a decent baking dish. The well-reviewed set (now 60% off!) includes pots and pans, bakeware, tinted glass prep bowls, wooden utensils, a trivet, spoon rest and pot holders — a whopping 23 pieces in total. Basically, it's a whole kitchen starter kit wrapped up in one very pretty package. "My one complaint about my air fryer is that it's not big enough to cook a frozen pizza," laments Senior Writer Carrie McCabe . "Well, OK, one more critique: It also takes up a bit more room than I'd like. So I've got my eye on this one from Ninja. It's roomy enough for a 12-inch pizza, flips up on its back (let it cool first!) to save counter space and can bake, toast, dehydrate and roast in addition to air frying. There are still great deals on everything from noise-canceling earbuds and e-readers to the latest smart mugs. Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. Between holiday travel, gifts, and the rising cost of just about everything, expenses can quickly add up during this time of year. Thankfully, you don’t have to dip too far into your savings to take advantage of some of the better Black Friday deals we’ve seen. Below, we’ve rounded up a range of great stuff currently on sale for $100 or less, from noise-canceling earbuds and portable Bluetooth speakers to pocket-sized e-readers , photo printers , games , and more. You’ll also find deals on Ember’s temperature-controlled mug , Kodak’s tiny keychain camera , and a variety of Lego sets , all of which would make great holiday gifts or simply a nice treat for yourself. You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons , Andor , Toy Story 5 , and The Fantastic Four: First Steps . Although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to. Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage. An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , The Last of Us , and The Pitt , as well as films like Superman and Weapons . You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st. The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review . You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review . Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too. Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps. 007 First Light , a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman , is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review . Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C. Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos. Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it. The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting. Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review . TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off. Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review . In Catan , up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood. Nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds have the same general design as the company’s previous earbuds — but you can get these in a snazzy yellow. They include ANC, more than decent sound quality, and other features like multipoint for well under $100. Read our impressions . Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time. Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four. With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app. The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip. No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port. The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review . Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan , but it is far more interesting. LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices. A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too. The Buds Pro 2 offer a surprisingly robust set of features for the price, including ANC and a transparency mode that lets you tune into your surroundings. Their included charging case also features a smart dial that lets you adjust the volume, while multipoint Bluetooth support lets them connect to two devices simultaneously. Fujifilm’s Instax Mini 13 is the best instant camera if you want to spend less than $100. While it lacks more advanced features, the simple instant camera takes good-quality shots quickly and easily and offers a built-in selfie mode along with a self-timer. It’s sold in a variety of fun colors that’ll especially appeal to kids and tweens. The Tile Pro is the company’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices. Camp Snap’s latest digital point-and-shoot camera may still lack a screen and capture only 8-megapixel stills, but it offers a slimmer design, faster performance, and filters right out of the box. That, along with several other new features, makes it easier for kids to use.

sources.title: Sleigh the holiday slump with Black Friday fitness deals on equipment we tested and love - New York Post
passages: Our New York Post shopping experts have decades of combined experience hunting for the biggest Black Friday and Cyber Monday savings on bestsellers across tech, beauty, clothing, home and more.
All year round, we test the latest and greatest products, diligently price-check and recommend only the best deals for your coin.

We research every “deal” to make sure mega sales aren’t just regular prices in disguise, and make sure you actually get the best discount on the web, while updating our coverage to reflect real-time trends and shopper needs.
Our deals only feature legitimate retailers that we actually recommend, so you never have to worry about scams.
You don’t have to spend a fortune to invest in your health.
Think discounted dumbbells, resistance bands, walking pads, supportive sneakers, performance leggings and more.
Black Friday is officially live at Best Buy !
Shop the sale now and score limited-time savings on fitness and wellness gadgets before the deals end Nov.
The Fitbit Inspire is loaded with step tracking, sleep insights, heart rate monitoring and stress management tools.

Vice President of Commerce Jackie Goldstein’s husband has used Fitbit devices for approximately eight years, sharing, “I originally bought it because I wanted to track my steps, but now I love the sleep tracking feature and the heart rate monitor for when I’m working out.” It’s an affordable wellness companion for anyone looking to build healthier habits.
Black Friday wearable deals are finally here.
Berk is a big fan of the COROS PACE 4, a performance-focused GPS watch that monitors heart rate, running pace and other essential fitness metrics.
Its impressive battery life offers up to 19 days of regular smartwatch use and up to 41 hours of GPS tracking, making it especially appealing for long-distance runners.

Whether you’re training for your next marathon, building a home gym, getting serious about strength training or simply looking for a little extra motivation to hit your daily step goal, there’s something worth shopping in this year’s Black Friday fitness sales.
Besides, January is just around the corner — which means now is the time to hone in on those fitness goals.
The sleek, fifth-generation ring is actually 40% smaller than previous models, so much so that I can barely feel it when wearing it.
Beyond sleep and activity tracking, its Symptom Radar gives me additional insights into my blood pressure and nighttime breathing.
It has even picked up on early signs of a cold before I noticed symptoms.
And as a parent, that data genuinely makes a difference.

As a health-forward member of Gen Z, Miska seeks out experts to weigh in on the benefits, safety and designs of both trending and tried-and-true fitness equipment, workout clothing, dietary supplements and more.
During Black Friday, Hypershells is dropping the price of the X Pro S to $799.
I’ve tested everything from buzzy vibration plate s and at-home Pilates equipment to bestselling running shoes and must-have activewear from Lululemon , Alo and more.

You’ll also find deals on Ember’s temperature-controlled mug , Kodak’s tiny keychain camera , and a variety of Lego sets , all of which would make great holiday gifts or simply a nice treat for yourself. You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons , Andor , Toy Story 5 , and The Fantastic Four: First Steps . Although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to. Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage. An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , The Last of Us , and The Pitt , as well as films like Superman and Weapons . You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st. The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review . You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review . Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too. Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps. 007 First Light , a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman , is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review . Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C. Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos. Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it. The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting. Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review . TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off. Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review . In Catan , up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood. Nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds have the same general design as the company’s previous earbuds — but you can get these in a snazzy yellow. They include ANC, more than decent sound quality, and other features like multipoint for well under $100. Read our impressions . Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time. Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four. With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app. The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip. No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port. The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review . Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan , but it is far more interesting. LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices. A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too. The Buds Pro 2 offer a surprisingly robust set of features for the price, including ANC and a transparency mode that lets you tune into your surroundings. Their included charging case also features a smart dial that lets you adjust the volume, while multipoint Bluetooth support lets them connect to two devices simultaneously. Fujifilm’s Instax Mini 13 is the best instant camera if you want to spend less than $100. While it lacks more advanced features, the simple instant camera takes good-quality shots quickly and easily and offers a built-in selfie mode along with a self-timer. It’s sold in a variety of fun colors that’ll especially appeal to kids and tweens. The Tile Pro is the company’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices. Camp Snap’s latest digital point-and-shoot camera may still lack a screen and capture only 8-megapixel stills, but it offers a slimmer design, faster performance, and filters right out of the box. That, along with several other new features, makes it easier for kids to use.

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , The Last of Us , and The Pitt , as well as films like Superman and Weapons . You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review .

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review .

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

007 First Light , a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman , is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review .

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review .

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review .

In Catan , up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds have the same general design as the company’s previous earbuds — but you can get these in a snazzy yellow. They include ANC, more than decent sound quality, and other features like multipoint for well under $100. Read our impressions .

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review .

Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan , but it is far more interesting.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

The Buds Pro 2 offer a surprisingly robust set of features for the price, including ANC and a transparency mode that lets you tune into your surroundings. Their included charging case also features a smart dial that lets you adjust the volume, while multipoint Bluetooth support lets them connect to two devices simultaneously.

Fujifilm’s Instax Mini 13 is the best instant camera if you want to spend less than $100. While it lacks more advanced features, the simple instant camera takes good-quality shots quickly and easily and offers a built-in selfie mode along with a self-timer. It’s sold in a variety of fun colors that’ll especially appeal to kids and tweens.

The Tile Pro is the company’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices.

Camp Snap’s latest digital point-and-shoot camera may still lack a screen and capture only 8-megapixel stills, but it offers a slimmer design, faster performance, and filters right out of the box. That, along with several other new features, makes it easier for kids to use.

Just don’t wait too long. Black Friday fitness deals from popular brands can sell out quickly, and some of the biggest discounts won’t stick around. All discounts are automatically applied at checkout Add a little extra resistance to every workout with Bala Bangles, the stylish, versatile weights that are as functional as they are fashionable. These Walito Fabric Resistance Bands are a must-have for anyone looking to strengthen their glutes, legs and core without investing in expensive gym equipment. Featuring five color-coded resistance levels, they’re comfortable, durable and designed to stay in place without rolling, pinching or digging into your skin. I love that they’re comfy and color-coded. I’ve genuinely noticed more muscle definition since adding them to my routine. Save 20% sitewide at Pvolve , plus score a FREE gift with qualifying bundle purchases! It even has a child-lock that adds peace of mind for parents like myself. It’s a great investment for improving cardiovascular fitness or simply getting up your step count. extraction.body: US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind. The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, would "support America's booming super intelligence economy". However, rival firm Amazon has criticised it as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan", while astronomers in the US said the move would "significantly undermine" the public's ability to study and observe the night sky. There is increasing opposition to data centres on earth, including in the US where experts say they were a factor in the Republicans big losses in the midterm elections. SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities". FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth". "This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said. Responding to the announcement, Musk wrote on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world." Under the FCC licence, deployment of the satellites must begin no later than November 2033. SpaceX will be required to have deployed 10% by November 2035, rising to 50% by November 2038. The company has already said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year. It is unclear whether a million satellites will indeed be launched or whether SpaceX has sought approval for a higher number than it will use. Like SpaceX's current Starlink network, which provides high-speed internet via more than 10,000 satellites, Starmind's satellites will operate in low-Earth orbit at altitudes ranging between 500-2,000km (310-1,242 miles). Starmind's satellites will communicate with Starlink's and then relay the data to Earth. Speaking to the Today programme, on BBC Radio 4, Prof Sir Martin Sweeting, founder and executive chairman of Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd, said while the idea of data centres in space seemed "technically feasible", whether it "makes sense at scale yet" still needed to be analysed. Being able to get the data from the network of satellites, he added, would depend on being able to use laser links from the ground to them. "That has not yet been perfected to the level at which it would be able to support the huge amounts of data that are likely to be transferred backwards and forwards," he said. Meanwhile, the American Astronomical Society (AAS) said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the decision. It said the proposed constellation would "significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities" as well as "the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky". sources.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
passages: SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.
The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles.
SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions.
The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document .

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.
The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues.
Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.” The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority. passages: The FCC gave SpaceX permission on November 25 to launch up to 1 million Starmind satellites, the first time the US has approved a constellation of data centers in space.
That sounds like a green light for Elon Musk’s plan to move AI computing into orbit, and in one sense it is.

But when I read the FCC’s order, I found it rules on far less than the headline suggests, because the agency set aside the biggest objections as outside its authority and postponed a decision that four of Starmind’s six orbital layers depend on.
So what is Starmind, why would anyone build a data center in space, and what’s still undecided?
SpaceX asked to send retired satellites above 600 km into far-away disposal orbits rather than burning them up in the atmosphere, and the FCC deferred that request.
I’d expect SpaceX’s first Starmind satellites to go there.
Each AI1 satellite carries a compute payload of up to 250 kilowatts at peak.

SpaceX argues that space solves both, since satellites in a sun-synchronous orbit (an orbit that keeps them in near-constant sunlight) get solar power without weather or grid connections, and heat can radiate into space without the chillers and cooling towers ground data centers need.
The scale is hard to picture, so I did the math.
For comparison, about 17,000 satellites are in orbit today, by Broadband Breakfast’s count.

extraction.body: SpaceX Starmind won FCC approval for up to 1 million AI data center satellites on November 25, 2026. You get the first US license for space-based data centers, but the FCC set aside heat and astronomy objections and still hasn't ruled on disposal above 600 km. The FCC gave SpaceX permission on November 25 to launch up to 1 million Starmind satellites, the first time the US has approved a constellation of data centers in space. That sounds like a green light for Elon Musk’s plan to move AI computing into orbit, and in one sense it is. But when I read the FCC’s order, I found it rules on far less than the headline suggests, because the agency set aside the biggest objections as outside its authority and postponed a decision that four of Starmind’s six orbital layers depend on. So what is Starmind, why would anyone build a data center in space, and what’s still undecided? SpaceX Starmind is a planned network of satellites that run AI computing chips in orbit and send the results back to Earth over laser links to Starlink, SpaceX’s internet satellites. Each satellite, called AI1, has a 75-meter wingspan of solar panels and a compute payload rated at up to 250 kilowatts at peak and 175 kilowatts on average, according to SpaceX’s Starmind page . SpaceX is designing that payload with Nvidia, as we covered when SpaceX and Nvidia announced the AI1 partnership , and says its Texas Gigasat Factory could start building the satellites as soon as late 2027. The scale is hard to picture, so I did the math. At 175 kilowatts each, a full constellation of 1 million satellites would draw about 175 gigawatts on average, roughly the output of 175 large nuclear reactors. For comparison, about 17,000 satellites are in orbit today, by Broadband Breakfast’s count. AI data centers on Earth are running into two limits, which are finding enough electricity and getting rid of heat. SpaceX argues that space solves both, since satellites in a sun-synchronous orbit (an orbit that keeps them in near-constant sunlight) get solar power without weather or grid connections, and heat can radiate into space without the chillers and cooling towers ground data centers need. The catch is that radiating heat in a vacuum takes very large radiators, and several people who commented to the FCC questioned whether orbital data centers can manage heat at all. SpaceX isn’t alone in betting they can. Blue Origin has asked the FCC for up to 51,600 satellites under its Project Sunrise, and Google is testing chips in orbit for its own Project Suncatcher, which we compared with SpaceX’s plan in our look at Google’s Project Suncatcher . The FCC says it’s still reviewing other orbital data center proposals. Amazon, Viasat and the American Astronomical Society all asked the FCC to deny the application, and Amazon called it “incomplete, speculative, and unrealistic” in its petition. The FCC’s answer, in its Memorandum Opinion and Order , is narrower than a ruling on the merits. The radio license itself covers Starmind’s backup and emergency links, since its main laser links fall outside the FCC’s jurisdiction. That framing shaped everything else. The astronomers argued that waste heat from a million satellites could raise the infrared glow of the sky and harm research, and the FCC replied that such “non-spectrum related impacts” are outside the scope of its review. Doubts about whether the technology works, or how it handles heat, got the same answer. For visible-light astronomy, the FCC relied on SpaceX’s commitment to coordinate with the National Science Foundation rather than adding conditions. In other words, these concerns weren’t resolved, they just weren’t the FCC’s to decide. My read is that the FCC’s pending ruling on satellite disposal matters more to Starmind’s real size than the 1 million figure does. SpaceX asked to send retired satellites above 600 km into far-away disposal orbits rather than burning them up in the atmosphere, and the FCC deferred that request. Four of Starmind’s six orbital layers sit above 600 km, so until that ruling comes, the most clearly usable space is the two lowest layers, including the sun-synchronous one between 565 and 585 km that suits a solar-powered satellite best. I’d expect SpaceX’s first Starmind satellites to go there. If the FCC approves the disposal plan, the limit shifts from regulators to launch costs and chip supply, which is where SpaceX’s Starship rocket and its Terafab chip factory plan come in. Starmind is SpaceX’s planned constellation of up to 1 million solar-powered satellites that run AI computing in orbit and send results to Earth through Starlink’s laser network. Each AI1 satellite carries a compute payload of up to 250 kilowatts at peak. The FCC requires SpaceX to have its first Starmind satellite operating by November 25, 2033, half the constellation by 2038 and all of it by 2040. SpaceX says manufacturing could start as soon as late 2027. Not yet. Starmind is the first orbital data center constellation the FCC has approved, and the agency says it’s still reviewing other proposals, including plans from Blue Origin and startups. Satellite operators sometimes request approval for higher numbers of satellites than they intend to deploy to buy design flexibility.
SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites before it began deployment of that system.
The growing network currently ​has more than 11,000 satellites in space.
Amazon's rival satellite unit Leo and ⁠others have criticized the plan, suggesting SpaceX was unlikely to deploy all the satellites ⁠and ⁠that it could take centuries ​to do so.
FCC Chair Brendan Carr rejected that criticism in March.
The FCC said it was approving the SpaceX “Starmind” constellation to help meet ​rapidly growing demand for AI computing.

"By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance costs, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and ⁠energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centres," SpaceX told the FCC.

coreStoryFacts.text: US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.
Under the FCC licence, deployment of the satellites must begin no later than November 2033.
SpaceX will be required to have deployed 10% by November 2035, rising to 50% by November 2038.

SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".

Like SpaceX's current Starlink network, which provides high-speed internet via more than 10,000 satellites, Starmind's satellites will operate in low-Earth orbit at altitudes ranging between 500-2,000km (310-1,242 miles).

Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney at the non-profit group Earthjustice, said in a statement: "Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people's everyday lives as well as the future of our planet."
The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.

SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.
The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles.
SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions.
The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document .

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.
The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues.
Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.
The FCC gave SpaceX permission on November 25 to launch up to 1 million Starmind satellites, the first time the US has approved a constellation of data centers in space.
That sounds like a green light for Elon Musk’s plan to move AI computing into orbit, and in one sense it is.

But when I read the FCC’s order, I found it rules on far less than the headline suggests, because the agency set aside the biggest objections as outside its authority and postponed a decision that four of Starmind’s six orbital layers depend on.
So what is Starmind, why would anyone build a data center in space, and what’s still undecided?
SpaceX asked to send retired satellites above 600 km into far-away disposal orbits rather than burning them up in the atmosphere, and the FCC deferred that request.
I’d expect SpaceX’s first Starmind satellites to go there.
Each AI1 satellite carries a compute payload of up to 250 kilowatts at peak.

SpaceX argues that space solves both, since satellites in a sun-synchronous orbit (an orbit that keeps them in near-constant sunlight) get solar power without weather or grid connections, and heat can radiate into space without the chillers and cooling towers ground data centers need.
For comparison, about 17,000 satellites are in orbit today, by Broadband Breakfast’s count.

extraction.body: US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind. The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, would "support America's booming super intelligence economy". However, rival firm Amazon has criticised it as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan", while astronomers in the US said the move would "significantly undermine" the public's ability to study and observe the night sky. There is increasing opposition to data centres on earth, including in the US where experts say they were a factor in the Republicans big losses in the midterm elections. SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities". FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth". "This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said. Responding to the announcement, Musk wrote on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world." Under the FCC licence, deployment of the satellites must begin no later than November 2033. SpaceX will be required to have deployed 10% by November 2035, rising to 50% by November 2038. The company has already said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year. It is unclear whether a million satellites will indeed be launched or whether SpaceX has sought approval for a higher number than it will use. Like SpaceX's current Starlink network, which provides high-speed internet via more than 10,000 satellites, Starmind's satellites will operate in low-Earth orbit at altitudes ranging between 500-2,000km (310-1,242 miles). Starmind's satellites will communicate with Starlink's and then relay the data to Earth. Speaking to the Today programme, on BBC Radio 4, Prof Sir Martin Sweeting, founder and executive chairman of Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd, said while the idea of data centres in space seemed "technically feasible", whether it "makes sense at scale yet" still needed to be analysed. Being able to get the data from the network of satellites, he added, would depend on being able to use laser links from the ground to them. "That has not yet been perfected to the level at which it would be able to support the huge amounts of data that are likely to be transferred backwards and forwards," he said. Meanwhile, the American Astronomical Society (AAS) said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the decision. It said the proposed constellation would "significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities" as well as "the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky". It noted that the constellation "involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects", meaning the satellites would "be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky". Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney at the non-profit group Earthjustice, said in a statement: "Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people's everyday lives as well as the future of our planet." The orbiting data centre concept is also being explored by other firms - including Google and Blue Origin - and is being pitched as a greener alternative to traditional centres, which require enormous amounts of power to run and water for cooling. The ever-expanding use of AI computing has seen a massive increase in the amount of data that needs to be stored and processed around the world. New facilities continue to be built but it is becoming difficult to find places to put them. Data centres are large and sprawling, use enormous amounts of power and water for cooling, and increasingly local people don't want them built nearby. Separately, another cautioned that the growing number of low-orbit craft increases the possibility of crashes between objects - which could damage machines or send materials falling back to earth. Starlink has been accused of creating congestion in space, something Musk denies. He has also rejected claims his satellites have been taking up too much room and crowding out competitors. Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remained badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain. No injuries were reported, and the FAA plans to investigate the incident, which occurred during taxiing. Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

sources.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
passages: SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.
The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles.
SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions.
The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document .

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.
The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues.
Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.
